unique_work_policy: One entry per unique primary work/version family; target conference report and manuscript are separately pinned source statements. Primary passage reads, expository reads, and metadata-only leads are labeled separately.

works.primary_work: Eran Nevo, Rigidity and the lower bound theorem for doubly Cohen–Macaulay complexes, Oberwolfach Report 17/2005
works.reading_scope: Definition 1, all-face Reisner statement, Theorem 7, Problem 8; text first, both rendered pages visually confirmed later.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: 2-CM over a fixed field; decomposition into minimal d-cycle complexes with d-face overlap and arbitrary first-piece reorderability; asks whether sphere pieces suffice.
works.exact_target_mapping: Original source of target, not a negative answer.

works.primary_work: Eran Nevo, Rigidity and the Lower Bound Theorem for Doubly Cohen-Macaulay Complexes
works.reading_scope: Definition 3.1 (p.4), Theorem 3.4 and proof (pp.6–7), Corollaries 3.5–3.6, Problem 3.7 and following CM-intersection discussion (pp.7–8).
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Same minimal-cycle decomposition and homology-sphere question; graph base case gives cycle covers.
works.exact_target_mapping: Confirms exact scope: same original finite complex, field fixed for 2-CM, full-dimensional sphere pieces. The graph case is positive and does not address dimension two.

works.primary_work: Alexander Lubotzky, Beth Samuels, Uzi Vishne, Explicit Constructions of Ramanujan Complexes
works.reading_scope: Introduction and Theorem 1.1, Section 2 lattice-chain definition, Section 3 conjugation embedding and Proposition 3.3 (p.9), Section 4 Corollary 4.6/Definition 4.7/Equation (9)/Proposition 4.8 (pp.12–13); text searched for Cohen, homology, sphere, girth.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Simply vertex-transitive Cartwright–Steger lattice, faithful conjugation matrices over F_q[1/y], and explicit finite building quotients. Equation (9) is linear in 1/y.
works.exact_target_mapping: Very substantial finite-quotient ingredient. For PGL_3 the building is two-dimensional and links are projective-plane incidence graphs. Its finite field is geometric; it does not specify the homology coefficient field. No read theorem asserts 2-CM after every vertex deletion plus absence of sphere subcomplexes. The Ramanujan theorem is unnecessary to the candidate.

works.primary_work: Alexander Lubotzky, Roy Meshulam, A Moore Bound for Simplicial Complexes
works.inspected_version: Author manuscript, 10 pages; journal publication 2007, BLMS 39, 353–358
works.reading_scope: Entire 10-page author manuscript, including Theorems A_d/B_d, Sections 3.1–3.2, Proposition 3.3 (p.7), proof of B_(d−1) (p.8), and concluding remarks.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Finite affine-building quotients with growing injectivity/acyclicity radius. Proposition 3.3 uses linear generator matrices in 1/y, degree bounds, congruence divisibility, and normality/transitivity. Theorem B_d gives (q+1)-regular d-complexes with logarithmic acyclicity radius.
works.exact_target_mapping: Closest directly recorded quotient mechanism found: the degree/congruence argument is already explicit here. Top homology and its support radius are not a homology-sphere subcomplex. No 2-CM or sphere-cover conclusion appears in this fully read short manuscript. Combining its quotients with deletion spectral estimates and Euler curvature would still be a new combination for this audit’s priority criterion.

works.primary_work: Werner Ballmann, Jacek Świątkowski, On L2-Cohomology and Property (T) for Automorphism Groups of Polyhedral Cell Complexes
works.reading_scope: Introduction Theorem 1, Corollary 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 2 (printed pp.1–3; PDF pp.3–5); Theorem 2.5 (printed p.12; PDF p.14); Sections 3.1–3.2 (printed pp.14–15; PDF pp.16–17); references. OCR is imperfect, threshold interpreted with the displayed normalized Laplacian definition.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Normalized vertex-link spectral gap above 1/2 implies first L2-cohomology vanishing in dimension two. Theorem 2 constructs contractible two-complexes with prescribed high-girth Cayley links and a proper cocompact group action; suitable expansion gives property T. Projective-plane link gap is 1−sqrt(m−1)/m.
works.exact_target_mapping: Spectral vanishing is already classical. Setting the acting group trivial applies to a finite pure complex. The source also records local girth and property T in the same broad setting, so these are not new mechanisms. Its read results do not give every vertex-deleted quotient, 2-CM over Q, or an explicit Nevo sphere-cover counterexample.

works.primary_work: Tadeusz Januszkiewicz, Jacek Świątkowski, Simplicial Nonpositive Curvature
works.reading_scope: Introduction Theorems A–D, Definition 1.1 and Fact 1.2 (pp.8–9), Examples 1.8(1)–(8) (pp.11–12), including the explicit 2-sphere Gauss–Bonnet non-example; text searched for CM, sphere, homology.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: The universal cover of a finite-dimensional connected locally 6-large complex is contractible. Example 1.8(5) explicitly uses combinatorial Gauss–Bonnet to exclude 6-large triangulations of the 2-sphere; Example 1.8(4) identifies affine A2 buildings as systolic.
works.exact_target_mapping: Strong prior local-curvature/sphere obstruction ingredient. The cited inheritance statement in Fact 1.2(2) concerns full subcomplexes; it cannot be silently applied to every arbitrary subcomplex. Candidate’s Euler incidence argument addresses arbitrary subcomplexes and all coefficient fields. No 2-CM finite quotient or full negative sphere-cover theorem was found in these passages.

works.primary_work: Ed Swartz, g-elements, Finite Buildings and Higher Cohen-Macaulay Connectivity
works.reading_scope: Introduction; Section 2 Definition 2.2, apartment construction and Theorem 2.3 (pp.4–7); Section 4 Theorem 4.1/proof and discussion through Problem 4.2 (pp.12–14).
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Finite spherical buildings have a convex ear decomposition; a complex with such a decomposition is doubly CM. The proof extends to all-face-link homology spheres and homology balls. The paper records (q+1)-CM connectivity for finite buildings associated to GF(q).
works.exact_target_mapping: A positive sphere/apartment-decomposition family, not an affine-building quotient theorem. Swartz fixes a finite Coxeter system and spherical apartments. The field GF(q) in the building is not a statement that every finite affine quotient is 2-CM over that field. Homology-sphere definition explicitly includes every face link.

works.primary_work: Izhar Oppenheim, Vanishing of Cohomology and Property (T) for Groups Acting on Weighted Simplicial Complexes
works.inspected_version: arXiv:1110.5724v5, 1 August 2014 (PDF internal generated date differs)
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Weighted/local spectral gap conditions imply cohomology vanishing and property T for contractible pure simplicial complexes with proper cocompact or more general actions.
works.exact_target_mapping: Refines the same classical vanishing family; contractible covering space and action hypotheses must be checked. It does not record the finite original-complex deletion conclusion or no-sphere conclusion in the read passages.

works.primary_work: Mihran Papikian, On Garland’s Vanishing Theorem for SL(n)
works.reading_scope: Introduction Theorem 1.1 (pp.1–2); Section 4 Theorem 4.4 and Remarks 4.5–4.6 (p.16); arithmetic quotient construction and Property T discussion (pp.17–18).
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Finite Bruhat–Tits quotients have vanishing real cohomology below top dimension for sufficiently large residue-field order; the arithmetic construction supplies finite quotients. Section 4.4 records the dimension-two >1/2 criterion.
works.exact_target_mapping: Confirms rational/real cohomology vanishing ingredients and original finite quotient context, but all vertex deletions and their links are not included in the stated quotient theorem. This is an expository source, not independent discovery evidence for Garland’s original result.

works.primary_work: Gunnar Fløystad, Enriched Homology and Cohomology Modules of Simplicial Complexes
works.reading_scope: Abstract/introduction; Section 1.6; Section 2.1 Theorem 2.1 and Remarks 2.2–2.3; Section 2.2 girth definition/Proposition 2.4 (pp.8–10).
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Algebraic characterizations of higher CM connectivity; links and joins preserve l-CM. Its simplicial girth is the least vertex-support degree of nonzero top enriched homology.
works.exact_target_mapping: This is not girth of vertex-link graphs. No theorem here supplies a finite two-dimensional l-CM complex with all link girths at least six or excludes homology-sphere covers in the read passages.

works.primary_work: Eric Babson, Volkmar Welker, Homological Algebra and Poset Versions of the Garland Method
works.reading_scope: Abstract/introduction; Theorem 2.2/Corollary 2.3 (pp.2–3); Section 6 in full (pp.16–22), including Conjectures 6.2/6.4 and Corollary 6.3; text searched for CM, sphere, buildings.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: General exactness criterion for a Garland structure; probabilistic vanishing for random simplicial and cubical quotient models, with cubical cohomology sometimes prescribed by the base torus.
works.exact_target_mapping: Current primary development of spectral machinery, including quotient/branched-cover models. These models include Δ-complex/cubical identifications and do not assert the target finite abstract simplicial complex, 2-CM after deletions, and all-field sphere exclusion.

works.primary_work: Uriya A. First, The Ramanujan Property for Simplicial Complexes
works.reading_scope: Abstract/introduction (pp.1–4); exact Theorem 7.22, Example 7.23 and proof opening (pp.85–86); text searched for CM, homology, sphere, girth.
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Arithmetic quotients of affine buildings of PGL_d(D) meeting stated compact-open and local hypotheses are completely Ramanujan; Example 7.23 describes high-dimensional Laplacian spectra.
works.exact_target_mapping: Stronger spectral quotient results than needed. Neither complete Ramanujan-ness nor geometric characteristic p alone is the all-deletions rational CM plus no-sphere statement. No full target recorded in inspected passages.

works.primary_work: Đỗ Trọng Hoàng, Nguyễn Công Minh, Trần Nam Trung, Cohen-Macaulay Graphs with Large Girth
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Classification concerns the Stanley–Reisner ring of the independence complex of a graph with large graph girth.
works.exact_target_mapping: Terminology false friend: graph girth is not the vertex-link girth of the candidate complex; CM refers to the independence complex. Excluded as an exact match.

works.primary_work: Alexander Lubotzky, Beth Samuels, Uzi Vishne, Division Algebras and Non-Commensurable Isospectral Manifolds
works.reading_scope: Abstract/introduction through Theorem 3 and version-scope discussion (pp.1–5).
works.strongest_relevant_recorded_result: Inspected v1 states compact real/complex locally symmetric manifold isospectrality results and explicitly focuses on characteristic-zero case.
works.exact_target_mapping: Search also returned an author-hosted later text with a finite-building-quotient Theorem 4. That later body was not acquired/read; its snippet is not evidence that v1 contains that theorem. Neither isospectrality statement itself is the target. Version access limit retained.
